question: A 32-year-old man who recently emigrated from Somalia comes to the physician because of a 4-week history of fever, cough, and chest pain. He has had a 5-kg (11-lb) weight loss over the last 3 months despite no changes in appetite. His temperature is 38.1°C (100.6°F). Physical examination shows enlarged cervical lymph nodes. The lungs are clear to auscultation. The results of an interferon-γ release assay are positive. An x-ray of the chest shows bilateral mediastinal lymphadenopathy. A transbronchial needle aspiration biopsy of a mediastinal lymph node is performed; a photomicrograph of the specimen is shown. The structure indicated by the arrow is most likely comprised of which of the following types of cells?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Positive interferon-γ release assay" -> "Suspicion of tuberculosis infection" -> "Mediastinal lymphadenopathy on chest x-ray" -> "Transbronchial needle aspiration biopsy performed" -> "Photomicrograph shows granuloma formation" -> "Granuloma likely comprised of macrophages" -> "Structure indicated by the arrow likely comprised of macrophages" -> 95%
analysis: Given the clinical presentation of fever, cough, chest pain, weight loss, positive interferon-γ release assay, and bilateral mediastinal lymphadenopathy, along with the photomicrograph showing a structure likely involved in granuloma formation, the cells indicated are most likely macrophages.
